---
title: "WTC First Responders Frailty Study"
---

## Overview

This ongoing study examines frailty trajectories among World Trade Center (WTC) first responders — a unique cohort with well-characterized environmental exposures and long-term health monitoring. As **lead biostatistician**, I am responsible for the full statistical analysis plan, modeling strategy, and results interpretation.

---

## Research Questions

- What is the **prevalence** of frailty in WTC first responders, and how has it changed over time?
- What are the key **predictors and risk factors** for frailty in this population?
- How does frailty relate to **downstream health outcomes** including hospitalizations, functional decline, and mortality?

---

## Study Design

**Longitudinal / repeated measures** — participants assessed at multiple time points, enabling analysis of frailty onset, progression, and reversal over time.

---

## Statistical Methods

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Descriptive statistics | Frailty prevalence and sample characteristics at each wave |
| Longitudinal regression | Frailty trajectories over time, adjusting for covariates |
| Mixed effects models | Within-person change accounting for repeated measures |
| Survival analysis | Time to frailty onset and frailty-related outcomes |
| Causal inference | Estimating effect of WTC exposures on frailty risk |

---
